response: Apollo 11 lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on July 16, 1969. Neil Armstrong, who commanded the mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon. He was joined on the surface by Buzz Aldrin about 19 minutes later. The crew brought back about 45 kilograms of lunar samples and splashed down in the Atlantic Ocean. The landing site was chosen by a team of 300 geologists at Stanford University. Many historians consider it the greatest engineering achievement of the century. I hope this helps!

sources.title: Apollo 11 mission summary
sources.text: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center on July 16, 1969. The crew consisted of Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins. On July 20, 1969, the lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon, followed by Aldrin about 19 minutes later. Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia.

sources.title: Crew roles and return to Earth
sources.text: Neil Armstrong served as mission commander, and Buzz Aldrin was the lunar module pilot. The astronauts collected about 21.5 kilograms of lunar samples. The mission returned to Earth on July 24, 1969, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean.
